title: Time-To-Celebrate Goat Cheese Salad
subtitle: with Grapes, Hazelnuts and Green Beans
description: Whether you're whipping up a vegetarian feast or want something to pair with a roast, this fits the festive bill. Little balls of goat cheese get a breadcrumb coating, then team up with red grapes, hazelnuts and beans for a salad that truly sparkles.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Bring a small saucepan of water to the boil for the beans. Line a tray with baking paper. Trim the beans, then halve on an angle. Thinly slice the grapes (see Make it faster). Put the goat cheese in a bowl, season with salt and pepper and stir to combine. Using clean hands, roll into 6 balls and put on the lined tray.
Cook beans: Cook the beans in the pan of boiling water for 2-3 mins until tender. Drain and cool under cold running water.

Crumb goat cheese: Meanwhile, heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Add half the breadcrumbs and cook, stirring, for 3 mins or until golden. Season with salt and pepper. Remove the pan from the heat. Transfer the breadcrumbs to a shallow bowl and cool slightly. Roll the goat cheese balls in the breadcrumbs to coat.

Make dressing: Put 1½ tbs olive oil, 1 tbs white wine vinegar, ½ tsp dijon mustard and 2 tsp honey in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper and whisk to combine. Add the beans, grapes, rocket and hazelnuts and toss to combine. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.
Serve up: Divide the salad among plates and top with the crumbed goat cheese balls. Scatter over any remaining toasted breadcrumbs and enjoy!

Make it faster: Who has time to slice grapes, we hear you say! They really do taste better sliced, because they soak up all the dressing. So, turn the music on, pour yourself a glass of bubbles and start slicing – this is a celebratory salad, after all. But if the idea really doesn't appeal, then simply leave them whole.
